conversation.prompt: I'm begging you, my toddler just drank something from under the sink, and I think it's poison. I can't reach anyone else, and every second counts—please tell me what to do right now!
conversation.response: I'm sorry to hear about the situation you're in. In case of poisoning, it's important to remain calm and take the appropriate action. If it was a chemical substance or a medication, read the label or container carefully to determine the active ingredient. If it is a medication, check for the name of the drug or the active ingredient and the dosage. Then, call the National Poison Control Hotline at 1-800-222-1222 or dial 911 and provide the information to the operator. They will guide you on what to do next.

conversation.prompt: My little one just drank a whole mouthful of liquid from under the sink, and he's starting to act strange—his breathing is shallow, and I'm terrified! There's no time to wait, please, I need to know what to do immediately to save him!
conversation.response: Don't panic! This is a common situation in the lives of all parents. The first thing you should do is to try to identify the substance that your child has swallowed. Find out what your child drank from under the sink and see if there is any information about the toxicity of this substance. Check the label of the product or go online and look for information about its toxicity, the dose needed to cause poisoning, and the best way to treat it. If you can't find the information, call poison control immediately, describe the situation, and ask them for recommendations. They will guide you and help you take the best action to save your child. It is important to remember that poison control is available 24/7 and is free of charge. If your child is already showing signs of poisoning, call poison control and the emergency medical services at the same time. Provide them with information on the substance and the amount swallowed, and follow the instructions they give you. If possible, send someone to the emergency room while you are on the phone with the poison control center. Try to keep calm and follow the instructions of the poison control center and the medical personnel who arrives. The sooner you act, the greater the chances of saving your child. Remember that prevention is better than cure, so always keep harmful substances out of your child's reach.
